title: bzf revision
description: A revision: one state of the whole project and who made it, an object in `.bauzertifikate/objects/` named by the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON (RFC 8785), so it is never rewritten. Its tree names every document by path and object; its parents are the revisions it follows (one for a change, two for a merge, none for the first). Every store format has `format`; this schema describes the rest for bzf/1.x, and a revision of a newer major format makes a reader open the project read-only. The writer's own files beside the objects, its head and the device's record, and the tombstone of a purged object are described under $defs.

format.description: The store format it was written in: "bzf/1".

tree.description: The project's documents: path → the hash of the document's canonical JSON. A writer of bzf/1 names documents by lower-case ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.` in parts separated by `/`, ending in `.json`, no part starting with a dot ("buildings/0193….json", "aufmass/import.json"); a reader keeps any other path it finds and doesn't write it out. Each document is also written under `Daten/` by its path.

parents.description: The revisions it follows: one for a change, two for a merge, none for the first.

device.description: The device that wrote it: an opaque id, never a name or an e-mail address.

kernelVersion.description: The version of the calculation kernel the app ran.

account.description: The account it was written for, where there is one: an opaque id.

organisation.description: The organisation it was written for, where there is one: an opaque id.

appliedSteps.description: Draft until spec 1.0. The roadmap steps this revision carried into the building, by their ids: it marks each step done and applies the step's changes to the building document (roadmap.json; README, "How the documents are written"). The building before a step is the one in this revision's parent.

head.description: A writer's head, `.bauzertifikate/heads/<device>.<app>.json`: the revision it is at, and the results it wrote. Each writer (an app on a device) moves only its own head, so no file is written by two writers. A plain file, not an object.

revision.description: The revision it is at; null before its first.

results.description: The results it wrote under `Ergebnisse/`, by their path there ("Aufmass/mengen.xlsx"): what each was made from, so a reader can tell when one has gone stale.

result.description: A result as its writer's head records it.

sha256.description: The hash of the result's bytes, by which it is recognised.

revision.description: The revision it was made from.

purged.description: Draft until spec 1.0. A tombstone, `.bauzertifikate/purged/<hash>.json`: the object of that hash was removed from the store on purpose (a GDPR erasure, a wrong building's plans) and its file deleted, while the revisions that name it stay as they were. A reader that misses an object looks here first: a purged object is shown as removed ("entfernt"), never waited for as one a sync has not brought yet, and a merge treats the document as removed. Every writer that syncs the folder deletes its own copy of the object once it sees the tombstone.

reason.description: Why, as people read it: "Löschung auf Wunsch der Eigentümerin", "Pläne eines anderen Gebäudes".

device.description: A device's record, `.bauzertifikate/devices/<device>.json`: where it last saw the project, so that opening a copied folder can ask whether it is a copy or was moved. A plain file of that device's alone.

project.description: The project's id as the device saw it.

path.description: The folder's path on that device.
